admin.signInClientSecretHint: Leave empty for a public client. A stored secret is never shown again.
admin.signInEnabledHint: The button appears once a test sign-in has passed with the current connection.
admin.signInFromEnvHint: Set by the KROMA_OIDC variables of this server's environment.
admin.signInGroupClaimHint: Where the provider lists a person's groups. A dotted path reads a nested claim, such as realm_access.roles.
admin.signInIssuerHint: The issuer URL your provider shows for the application. Replace anything in capitals with your own value. It must be https, or a host on your local network.
admin.signInLeaveMessage: Your sign-in changes are not saved.
admin.signInMethodsHint: The sign-in screen offers these from top to bottom. Add an OpenID Connect provider such as Keycloak, Authentik or Microsoft Entra ID to put its button there.
admin.signInNameHint: The sign-in button reads "Continue with" and this name.
admin.signInNewAskHint: A person this server has never seen files a join request. You approve it under Users, and choose what they can do and see.
admin.signInNewCreateHint: Anyone the provider lets through gets an account at once, with the permissions and libraries below. Restrict who can reach the application at the provider, or require a group.
admin.signInNewInviteHint: A person this server has never seen is turned away unless they open an invitation link first.
admin.signInPasskeysHint: A fingerprint, a face or a security key, with nothing to type.
admin.signInPasswordHint: An email or a username, and a password. Whoever can change these settings keeps theirs when this is off.
admin.signInPasswordLocked: Stays on until a provider is live, so nobody is locked out.
admin.signInPresetAuthelia: Tested with Authelia 4.39. KROMA has to trust Authelia's certificate. To send groups, list groups among the client's scopes.
admin.signInPresetAuthentik: Tested with Authentik 2025.10. Give the provider a signing key, or its tokens are refused. Groups arrive with the profile scope.
admin.signInPresetCasdoor: Tested with Casdoor 4.27. A group arrives written organisation/group.
admin.signInPresetFusionauth: Tested with FusionAuth 1.70. Set the tenant's issuer to this address and choose an RSA or EC key for the application's ID token, or its tokens are refused.
admin.signInPresetHint: Fills this form with what the provider starts from, and sets the button's logo and look. Any OpenID Connect provider works.
admin.signInPresetKeycloak: Tested with Keycloak 26. To send groups, add a Group Membership mapper named groups to the client.
admin.signInPresetLogto: Tested with Logto 1.46. A person's roles arrive as groups.
admin.signInPresetNextcloud: Tested with Nextcloud 35 and its OIDC Identity Provider app 2.6. Groups need no setup.
admin.signInPresetPocketId: Tested with Pocket ID 2.19. A new client lets nobody in until you allow all users, or the groups you choose, on it.
admin.signInPresetRauthy: Tested with Rauthy 0.37. Keep the slash at the end of the address.
admin.signInPreviewHint: What people see once you save. Nothing here can be pressed.
admin.signInPreviewWaiting: Not shown yet: {names}. A provider appears after a test sign-in passes.
admin.signInProvidersHint: OpenID Connect providers such as Authentik, Keycloak, Pocket ID or Microsoft Entra ID. Each one adds a button to the sign-in screen.
admin.signInRedirectHint: Register this address at your provider as the redirect URI of the KROMA application.
admin.signInRequiredGroupsHint: Press Enter or type a comma after each name. A person must be in one of them at every sign-in. Run a test sign-in to see the exact names your provider sends.
admin.signInScopesHint: Asked for on top of openid, profile and email. Press Enter or Space after each one. The groups scope is added by itself when the provider offers it.
admin.signInSub: Choose how people get into this server.
admin.signInTestAdmitted: This person would be let in.
admin.signInTestNotAdmitted: This person is in none of the required groups and would be refused.
